answer: Registration binds each agent identity to a 300-unit bond escrowed against one hardware key, and each key registers once, recorded in a lagoon ledger. An attacker staking N fakes locks 300N units, loses 100 percent of bond on detection, and waits 30 epochs to withdraw. Splitting identities raises marginal cost per fake, since a shared vertex penalty propagates to all linked keys and independent raven jurors flag duplicates.
